notes:
RES-001 (blocking), repaired. Augustine, In Ioh. ev. tract. 48.4 was re-read in the tracked NPNF vol. 7 (section 4, physical lines 21499-21514). research/interpretations.md, Reading 2 two-peoples, now reports it only for what it says. The first element is the gloss on John 10:26 ("That He saw them predestined to everlasting destruction, not won to eternal life by the price of His own blood"). The second is the exhortation "be ye sheep", addressed to his own congregation, who "have already learned above (in Lecture XLV.) who the sheep are". The Author evidence row now marks him as the contrary position; he does not carry the claim. The gospel-acclamation row lists him as the contrary position. It rests the contribution on Aquinas on 10:26 and Gregory on 10:16, each with his own qualification, re-read on the Venice 1745 p. 668 page image and in the tracked Gregory text. Aquinas first glosses 10:26 as Augustine does ('praesciti ad aeternum interitum'). He then distinguishes within the crowd: none were then preordained to believe, some were preordained to believe later, and the saying was spoken to a crowd and to no determinate person. Gregory's one fold is made of those chosen 'ex utraque natione', at 10:16, and he says nothing of 10:26. The 'A second difference' paragraph was rewritten to match. research/scope.md 3.5 (the Augustine, Gregory and Aquinas rows and the paragraph after them) and section 7 were corrected the same way. No wording is left that has Augustine calling the unbelievers of 10:26 to become sheep.

summary: Repaired RES-001. The two-peoples records now report Augustine's tract. 48.4 as a gloss that those addressed at John 10:26 were predestined to destruction, beside an exhortation to his own congregation, and list him as the contrary position. Aquinas on 10:26 and Gregory on 10:16 now carry the acclamation contribution with their own re-read qualifications. Advisories RES-002 to RES-007 were cleared in the same files, with new bindings, a new dated USCCB page state and Nostra aetate 4 checked; all research gates pass.
